name: FRED 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average (MORTGAGE30US)
measures: Weekly average 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgage rate in the US, from Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS), published on FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis).
history: Back to April 1971, weekly. Ample history for percentile/range statistics and for backtest-style analysis of how rate regime affected past appreciation periods.
license: Free. Requires a no-cost FRED API key (email registration, same shape as CENSUS_API_KEY already required by app/sources/census_acs.py). FRED's own terms of use explicitly permit only non-commercial, educational, and personal use without extra restriction, and state commercial use carries 'additional restrictions' -- FRED's published terms do not spell out what those are for this specific series, and that page (fred.stlouisfed.org) was egress-blocked from this research environment, so it could not be read directly. Checked the original source instead: Freddie Mac publishes PMMS data itself at freddiemac.com/pmms under a copyright notice permitting use 'with proper attribution' (alteration prohibited, no warranty) -- suggestive but not an explicit commercial/product-use grant either. COMMERCIAL-USE TERMS UNVERIFIED; review both FRED's and Freddie Mac's terms directly (and consider going straight to freddiemac.com/pmms, which appears to need no API key at all, instead of the FRED API) before implementing.
rate_limits: FRED API: no published hard rate limit for reasonable use with a registered key; weekly-cadence polling is trivially within any reasonable limit.
correlation: Not computed -- app/research/evaluate_series.py (Phase 4) does not exist yet in this repo. Recommend running the standard correlation/lead-lag check against FHFA tract HPI growth once that tool is built; historically, mortgage-rate regime has an obvious economic linkage to affordability and appreciation, but this is asserted from domain knowledge, not measured here.
existing_overlap: None. Searched backend/app/scoring/investment.py: `Assumptions.interest_rate` is a hardcoded default (0.065) with no data source feeding it -- confirmed via `grep -in rate backend/app/scoring/investment.py`. No FRED source exists anywhere in app/sources/ or sources.yaml today.
recommendation_notes: This is the clearest concrete gap found this run: the investment engine's loan-cost assumption (interest_rate=0.065, backend/app/scoring/investment.py:21) is a static constant that goes stale as soon as market rates move, and every IRR/cash-flow projection depends on it. A weekly pull would let that default track reality and let the assumptions UI show 'as of <date>, currently X%' instead of a hardcoded number. Architecturally this does NOT fit the existing `neighborhood`/`sales`/`listings`/`sold_check` Source kinds -- it is one national scalar, not a per-NTA metric -- so it needs either (a) a new lightweight `MacroSeries`-style table + a new source `kind`, or (b) folding into the `app/valuation/` engine's planned `FactorDef.market_estimate()` mechanism once that module exists (backend/CLAUDE.md already specifies market_estimate() must return P10/P90 range + source + as-of date, which 50+ years of weekly MORTGAGE30US history supports well). Downgraded from a flat 'recommend' to 'recommend-with-caveats' because commercial/product-use licensing terms could not be conclusively verified this run (fred.stlouisfed.org was egress-blocked here, and Freddie Mac's own PMMS page only confirms 'use with attribution', not an explicit commercial grant) -- confirm terms directly before implementing, and evaluate freddiemac.com/pmms as a keyless alternative to the FRED API.
